historic claim did not reproduce as stated, the honest number is here instead._

## 1. Method, before numbers

**One recipe per instrument** — what CI or a reviewer runs is what produced the tables here.
**Committed artifacts are the ground truth** — a PR that changes a number changes an artifact,
so the diff *is* the claim review; tables and markers are generated, the prose is hand-written.
**Enforcement over aspiration** — the same typed e2e harness that measures the headline asserts
it under a budget on every commit (`crates/swath-e2e`, `I2P_BUDGET_MS`); the other baselines are
regression evidence: re-run, diff, explain movement.

## 2. Environment (full disclosure)

One developer laptop: Apple M2 Max (12 logical cores, 32 GB RAM), macOS 26.5.2 arm64;
rustc 1.97.1 (criterion on the optimized `bench` profile; e2e/load hit the release binary in a
`debian:trixie-slim` linux/arm64 container — Docker Engine 29.3.1, Compose v5.1.1); oha 1.15.0
(version-pinned) plus a unique-URL Python driver for the cold burst; Python 3.13.5 via uv, pins
from `python/uv.lock`. Serve dataset: the committed HLS fixtures (`tests/fixtures/`, ~1.4 MB,
real swath-edge nodata). Referencer dataset: the pinned VNP09GA conformance granule (8.2 MB
HDF-EOS5, 1,551 chunk refs — ADR 0008). Not controlled: thermal state, background processes,
page cache — "cold" means "first run in the recipe invocation", not cold-boot. A laptop, not a
lab.

## 3. Instruments: which recipe, which artifact

The stamp table above maps each instrument to its recipe and artifact. Methodology lives with
each instrument: the i2p harness in `crates/swath-e2e` (§4), the criterion benches beside the
crates they measure (§5), the load scenarios in `tests/load/load.{sh,py}` (§6), the referencer
bake-off in the `perf-referencer` recipe (§7), and the temporal/overview scenarios in
`tests/load/temporal.{sh,py}` (§8).

## 4. Ingest-to-pixel (the headline)

The north-star metric (REQUIREMENTS §3), measured end to end through the real stack by the same
harness that verifies the tile's pixels against goldens.

<!-- table:i2p (generated by `just perf-doc` — edit the artifact, not this block) -->
| metric | measured | enforced budget |
|---|---:|---:|
| ingest_to_pixel_ms | 646 ms | 10000 ms |
<!-- /table:i2p -->

**Enforcement.** `just e2e` asserts `ingest_to_pixel_ms` under the 10,000 ms budget on every
commit; the budget is deliberately ~20× above measured values so it catches structural
regressions rather than runner noise, and tightening it is a deliberate, visible act.

Single-request tile latency under no load is visible in the load table below (cold live renders:
p50 <!-- number:cold-p50-approx -->~660 ms<!-- /number:cold-p50-approx --> for z15 tiles; hot cache hits: p50 <!-- number:hot-p50-approx -->~23 ms<!-- /number:hot-p50-approx --> at c=32 — see §6).

## 6. Concurrency and the async-vs-blocking boundary

`just load` is the concurrency measurement the e2e never takes (ARCHITECTURE §16.7). All
scenarios run against the containerized release binary over loopback HTTP:

<!-- table:load (generated by `just perf-doc` — edit the artifact, not this block) -->
| scenario | requests | errors | rps | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | max ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| healthz — idle baseline | 84450 | 0 | 16883.2 | 0.23 | 0.3 | 0.36 | 3.84 |
| (a) hot-cache tile storm | 26306 | 0 | 1313.7 | 23.33 | 34.91 | 41.79 | 72.57 |
| (b) cold live-render burst | 128 | 0 | 11.5 | 660.61 | 1140.7 | 1221.21 | 1231.08 |
| (c) mixed tile storm | 813 | 0 | 20.1 | 852.82 | 1983.87 | 2051.72 | 2096.35 |
| (c) healthz UNDER WARPS | 190707 | 0 | 9533.8 | 0.39 | 0.64 | 0.97 | 30.35 |

SSE `/traces` under the mixed storm: survived the 45s window: **yes** (828 trace events received).
<!-- /table:load -->

The §16.7 evidence is the last two rows: under c=16 clients hammering the heaviest live warps,
`/healthz` p99 stays sub-millisecond and the SSE subscription survives — blocking render work is
not starving the async control plane.

## 7. Referencer: the historic "40×" and "14 ms" claims, re-run

**Provenance.** Prototype 0001 (immutable) measured generation on the VNP09GA granule:
*"referencer-rs 29 ms cold / 14 ms warm; virtualizarr sidecar 876 ms cold / ~556–574 ms warm …
Rust ≤ sidecar by ~40× warm."* — the Rust generator timed **in-process** (dev profile), the
sidecar **as a subprocess**. **Re-measurement on this tree**: `just perf-referencer` measures
the production generator and the promoted conformance sidecar the same way — full-process wall
clock, release profile, same granule — which is *less* flattering to Rust:

<!-- table:referencer (generated by `just perf-doc` — edit the artifact, not this block) -->
| generator | command | cold | warm (median) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| referencer-rs | `target/release/swath ingest reference <path-to>/VNP09GA.A2012019.h33v12.002.2023122182434.h5 --output target/referencer/perf-rs.vmanifest.json` | 456.2 ms | 13.8 ms |
| virtualizarr-sidecar | `python/.venv/bin/swath-referencer <path-to>/VNP09GA.A2012019.h33v12.002.2023122182434.h5` | 13278.0 ms | 545.6 ms |

Warm-generation ratio (sidecar / Rust): **~39.5x** in Rust's favor (10 runs; full-process wall clock; run 1 = cold, warm = median of the rest).
<!-- /table:referencer -->

**Verdicts** (all 10 raw samples in the artifact):

- **"14 ms warm" — reproduces.** Warm median <!-- number:ref-warm-ms -->13.8 ms<!-- /number:ref-warm-ms --> for the production release binary,
  full-process (the release-profile speedup and the added process overhead happen to cancel).
- **"~40× warm" — reproduces.** Sidecar warm median <!-- number:ref-sidecar-warm-ms -->545.6 ms<!-- /number:ref-sidecar-warm-ms --> / Rust <!-- number:ref-warm-ms -->13.8 ms<!-- /number:ref-warm-ms --> = **<!-- number:ref-ratio -->39.5×<!-- /number:ref-ratio -->**, squarely
  in line with the prototype's ~40×.
- **The cold numbers are NOT comparable to the prototype's and we don't headline them.** Both are
  first-invocation-after-build effects (binary first-touch + code-signature verification; one-time
  bytecode compilation of a fresh venv). Steady-state (warm) is the operationally meaningful
  figure for a per-granule ingest step, and it is the one we claim.

Both generators emit byte-range-equivalent manifests — that equivalence is the gated
conformance test (`just test-referencer`), so the comparison is between implementations
producing verified-identical output.

**Honest accounting of the ratio.** The sidecar's per-invocation cost is dominated by Python
interpreter + import time, and production runs the generator per granule as a process — so
per-invocation is the operationally honest unit. But stated plainly: this is an architecture
result (no interpreter, no warm-up, a 4.5 MB static binary vs a ~273 MB venv), not a claim that
Rust scans HDF5 chunk indexes <!-- number:ref-ratio-approx -->~40×<!-- /number:ref-ratio-approx --> faster than h5py once Python is already warm.

## 8. Temporal frame-serving and overview-backed tiles

The M7 measurement (`just load-temporal`): the time slider's serving path (ADR 0015, issue #223)
and the materialized overview path (`swath materialize`, issues #183/#218), on the §2 laptop and
compose stack plus the six-date Park Fire fixture series dropped mid-run. Every request's render
decision is recorded, and the report *fails* unless the decision mix is exactly what each
scenario is defined by — the latencies below are proven to be the paths they claim to measure.

**(d) Animation frames** — every interior z14 tile of the fire footprint, requested with
`datetime=` for each of the six dates in order: cold (fresh tile cache, every dated frame a live
render) p50 <!-- number:frame-cold-p50-approx -->~350 ms<!-- /number:frame-cold-p50-approx -->
per tile; the same loop again is all granule-scoped cache hits at p50
<!-- number:frame-hot-p50-approx -->~8 ms<!-- /number:frame-hot-p50-approx --> — the temporal
cache identity (granule id, not the datetime string) is what makes a replayed animation cheap.

**(e) The overview ladder** — one tile per zoom rung, tile cache cleared before every request,
so each rung measures its *render* path: z12 plans full-resolution live (p50
<!-- number:ov-live-p50-approx -->~260 ms<!-- /number:ov-live-p50-approx -->); pre-materialize,
z10 serves the fixtures' embedded ×2 overview; after `swath materialize`
(<!-- number:materialize-ms -->578 ms<!-- /number:materialize-ms --> for every layer of both
datasets, run mid-scenario) the same z10 tile plans the materialized ×4 pyramid level at p50
<!-- number:ov-pyramid-p50-approx -->~130 ms<!-- /number:ov-pyramid-p50-approx -->. The overview
*level* served by each rung is pinned from the SSE trace envelopes.

<!-- table:temporal (generated by `just perf-doc` — edit the artifact, not this block) -->
| scenario | requests | errors | rps | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | max ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (d) frame loop, cold (all Live) | 54 | 0 | 14.6 | 345.99 | 606.77 | 619.69 | 619.69 |
| (d) frame loop, hot (all cache hits) | 54 | 0 | 150.7 | 7.91 | 270.43 | 271.12 | 271.12 |
| (e) z12 — Live (full resolution) | 24 | 0 | 3.7 | 259.24 | 269.31 | 288.11 | 288.11 |
| (e) z10 pre-materialize (embedded ov. ×2) | 24 | 0 | 4.0 | 230.59 | 257.88 | 290.6 | 290.6 |
| (e) z11 post-materialize (pyramid ov. ×2) | 24 | 0 | 3.7 | 246.59 | 296.56 | 317.68 | 317.68 |
| (e) z10 post-materialize (pyramid ov. ×4) | 24 | 0 | 6.6 | 134.75 | 146.19 | 162.52 | 162.52 |

Frame decisions (`x-swath-trace`): cold {"live": 54}, hot {"cache_hit": 54}. Overview-rung decisions (SSE envelopes, level included): live_z12 {"live": 24}; embedded_z10 {"overview:2": 24}; pyramid_z11 {"overview:2": 24}; pyramid_z10 {"overview:4": 24}.
<!-- /table:temporal -->

A dated frame pays the ordinary live price on first touch and the ordinary cache-hit price on
replay; the materialized ×4 level reads a quarter the pixels of the embedded ×2 fallback.

## 9. What we don't claim

Bounded honesty, in the spirit of the requirements' "reports it continuously and honestly":

**Fixture scale** (~1.4 MB of fixtures, one 8 MB granule — nothing about multi-terabyte
catalogs or granules that dwarf RAM); **single node, loopback** (no TLS/CDN/scaling claims);
**local storage**; **tested concurrency only** (up to c=32, seconds-to-minutes windows);
**microbenches are isolated stages** (no queueing or concurrent-warp interference — §6 samples
that); **one machine, uncontrolled** (diff same-machine baselines only); **the
<!-- number:ref-ratio-approx -->~40×<!-- /number:ref-ratio-approx --> ratio is per-invocation,
one granule, one format** (§7's accounting); **CI runners are slower and noisier** (the 10 s
enforcement budget is sized for that).

Several of these gaps are intended future work, not permanent posture — real-ingress behavior,
multi-node scale, and larger-than-fixture datasets are on the M7+ candidate list in
[`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md).

## 10. Regenerating this document

```bash
just bench-baseline    # re-run all criterion benches, rewrite docs/perf/bench-baseline.json
just load              # bring up the stack, run load scenarios, rewrite docs/perf/load-baseline.{json,md}
just load-temporal     # fire-series frame loop + overview ladder, rewrite docs/perf/temporal-baseline.{json,md}
just perf-i2p          # run the typed e2e, commit its metrics as docs/perf/i2p-baseline.json
just perf-referencer   # re-measure the referencer bake-off, rewrite docs/perf/referencer-baseline.json
just perf-doc          # regenerate every table above AND every inline number marker across the docs
```

Commit the artifact diffs alongside the regenerated tables; the PR should say why numbers moved.
Headline figures quoted in prose live inside inline `number:<key>` HTML-comment marker pairs;
`just perf-doc` fills every marker from the committed artifacts (idempotent), and the docs-check gate verifies each marker's
content and rejects any naked headline literal outside a marker
(`crates/swath-cli/src/docs_check/numbers.rs`). To quote a headline number, add a marker with an
existing key and run `just perf-doc`; never type the number by hand.
